findings.title: Stand-down blocks vanilla casting for player pawns the driver will not act for
findings.detail: ControlOf returns Player for any player pawn with at least one autocast mode set (AbilityAI.cs:556), so Handles is true and the AICanTargetNow postfix (AbilityAIMod.cs:90) tells vanilla no. But CanActNowPlayer returns false whenever the pawn is undrafted or moving (AbilityAI.cs:590-591), so the driver never casts it either, and the ability goes unused in every case where vanilla's GetAbilityJob / JobGiver_NPCCastNonCombatAbilities would have cast it. One change at the postfix: for Control.Player, only stand vanilla down while the pawn is drafted (the only state where autocast can fire), e.g. `if (__instance.pawn.Faction?.IsPlayer == true && !__instance.pawn.Drafted) return;` before calling Handles.

findings.title: TryGiveJob commits cooldowns, NotifyCast and the AttackStatic resume clone before vanilla accepts the job
findings.detail: Source/AbilityAI/AbilityAI.cs TryGiveJob sets state.nextCastTick/abilityNext, calls AbilityAIHooks.NotifyCast and EnqueueFirst(resume) before returning the job. Vanilla can still discard it: CheckForJobOverride with minPriority>0 needs SourceNode.TryGetPriority, and the constant tree's root (the SourceNode used here) has no priority, so the job is returned to the pool (Pawn_JobTracker.cs:580). The resume clone then stays queued and the attack repeats once. The only such caller is JobDriver_Reading.cs:139, so this is rare. One option: enqueue the resume only for drafted pawns whose CurJob is AttackStatic, and only on the JobTrackerTickInterval path. Or accept it and keep the existing hook caveat.

findings.title: Handles reads only the first AbilityAIExtension while the driver tries all of them
findings.detail: AbilityAIDriver.Handles uses def.GetModExtension<AbilityAIExtension>() and returns false if that one's Worker is null. TryGiveJob iterates every AbilityAIExtension in def.modExtensions. If the first extension has a bad workerClass and a later one is valid, this mod casts the ability but the stand-down does not tell vanilla to step aside. ConfigErrors already flags the bad extension at load, so this only matters for a broken def.

findings.title: Stand-down also answers other mods' bespoke AIs that call Ability.AICanTargetNow
findings.detail: Mods such as Apex Mechanoids gate their own job givers on ability.AICanTargetNow. For any ability that carries an AbilityAIExtension and is handled, those job givers now get false as well. This matches the documented intent (the host's fallback steps aside) and only affects abilities that hosts give an extension, but it is worth knowing when a host's own AI stops casting.

findings.title: GizmoOnGUI prefix uses up every right-click on ability gizmos that have an AI extension
findings.detail: ev.Use() on MouseDown button 1 means any RightClickFloatMenuOptions another mod adds to such a Command_Ability will never open. Vanilla's Command_Ability adds none (only Command_Hide among vanilla Commands has them), and no mod in the corpus patches Command_Ability, so nothing breaks today.

findings.title: Saved autocast entries for a removed AbilityDef log a load error
findings.detail: Scribe_Defs.Look on an AbilityDef whose mod was removed logs vanilla's 'Could not load reference' error once on load. The entry is then dropped by the null check in PostLoadInit, so the save still loads. This is the same as vanilla's handling of removed defs.

findings.title: Per-AbilityDef effects cache is not cleared by AbilityAIInfo.Register
findings.detail: AbilityAIUtility.EffectsOf caches stuns/hediff/psychic per AbilityDef in a static dictionary, partly from AbilityAIInfo.Of. AbilityAIInfo.Register clears its own cache (Source/AbilityAIInfo.cs:47) but not this one. A host that registers after any worker has evaluated a def would keep stale skipAffected answers. Registering before play, as documented, avoids it. Clearing `effects` from Register (an internal Clear hook) would make the 'registering clears it' promise true for both caches.

findings.title: 1.7 assembly compiles against a prerelease ref package but cannot be run on this machine
findings.detail: 1.7/Source/AbilityAI.csproj references UnityStubs.dll and Waylith.dll from Krafs.Rimworld.Ref 1.7.4979-alpha by path, matching EntadFramework/1.7/Source/EntadFramework.csproj line for line. The installed game is 1.6, so a green build only shows the 1.7 DLL compiles, not that it loads. 1.7/Assemblies also has AbilityAI.pdb from a Debug build. Whether the stub assemblies resolve at runtime on 1.7 could not be checked: the package folder is outside the readable paths.

findings.title: minRange is honoured by TargetHostile only; Interrupt, TargetFriendly, Defensive, Rescue and Calm ignore it
findings.detail: AbilityAIExtension documents minRange as the 'Distance band from the caster to the target or threat' for workers generally (AbilityAI.cs:163-164), but only AbilityAIWorker_TargetHostile.Score filters on it (line 97). Interrupt (around line 309) filters on maxSq alone, so an XML author who sets minRange on an interrupt or buff ability gets no effect and no warning. Either add the `d < minSq` check in Interrupt's loop, which is the one hostile worker here without it, or narrow the doc comment to say which workers read it.

findings.title: Defensive: minThreats 0 makes every ally in range count as 'in trouble'
findings.detail: InTrouble returns true when AimedAtCount + RecentlyShot >= ext.minThreats, before the health check. With the default of 1 (AbilityAI.cs:180) this is correct. If a def sets minThreats to 0, 0 >= 0 holds for every ally, so Invisibility-type abilities would be cast on anyone in range whenever the worker runs. A `ext.minThreats > 0 &&` guard on that line closes it.
